summary:
Beyond the Mission is a responsive educational app that connects spacecraft, destinations, hardware, discoveries, images, maps, and mission videos.

It has four main sections: Home introduces the project and features search; Hardware lets visitors browse spacecraft by name, destination, agency, mission type, or status; Terrain Explorer covers rocky worlds, giant planets, and small bodies or comets; and About explains the project’s sources and limits.

The app includes 20 spacecraft profiles: Kepler, NEOWISE, Geotail, InSight, Dawn, Ulysses, Opportunity, Spirit, Deep Impact, Stardust, Phoenix, MAVEN, Nozomi, AIM, MESSENGER, Cassini, Huygens, Galileo, Voyager 1, and Voyager 2. Each profile includes the mission purpose, hardware, discoveries, timeline-based story, status, video links, and sources.

The Terrain Explorer covers 13 worlds. Rocky worlds have image maps with explanations of their data and limitations. Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune are explored through their atmospheres, rings, moons, and spacecraft observations rather than solid-surface maps. Ceres, Vesta, and three comets have encounter records, field notes, and source-linked findings.

Beyond the Mission is an educational web app that brings spacecraft, destinations, mission histories, and scientific findings into one interactive guide. It was built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, without a separate build step. The responsive interface includes Home, Hardware, Terrain Explorer, and About sections, with search and filters to help visitors explore the catalog.

The app contains profiles and interactive 3D model pages for 20 spacecraft: Kepler, NEOWISE, Geotail, InSight, Dawn, Ulysses, Opportunity, Spirit, Deep Impact, Stardust, Phoenix, MAVEN, Nozomi, AIM, MESSENGER, Cassini, Huygens, Galileo, Voyager 1, and Voyager 2. Mission pages bring together each craft’s purpose, hardware, timeline, story, discoveries, videos, and references. The models use a shared compact control bar, with mission-specific controls where available.

Terrain Explorer covers 13 worlds: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Ceres, Vesta, Comet Wild 2, Comet Tempel 1, and Comet Hartley 2. It combines planetary image maps, terrain notes, spacecraft observations, and source-linked findings. Giant planets are presented through their atmospheres, rings, and moons because they do not have solid surfaces like rocky worlds.

The research draws on the supplied spacecraft paper and video directory, alongside public mission information from NASA, NASA/JPL, ESA, and JAXA. NASA image and video services provide additional media when online. Sources and credits are linked in the app. The 3D scenes are illustrative project models, not verified engineering geometry or live telemetry. The project is independent and is not an official NASA product.
